category: SEC Football — It Just Means More
prompt: Your wedding was scheduled the same day as the Georgia-Florida game. Explain to your fiancée why the venue has TVs now.
response:
Look, I love you. I'm marrying you. That's the whole point of this day.

But here's the thing—I invited a lot of people who love us, and some of those people made a real sacrifice to be here instead of watching the game live. Uncle Ray drove four hours. My college roommates rearranged their whole weekend. These are the folks who'll be dancing with us at the reception and telling embarrassing stories about me for the next forty years.

So I got a couple of TVs set up in the corner of the reception hall. Not the ceremony—I'd never. During the ceremony every phone is off and every eye is on you. That part is sacred.

But at the reception, when we're eating and the band's on break? Letting people peek at the score keeps everyone happy and present. Nobody's sneaking off to the parking lot to stream it on their phone. Nobody's checking updates under the table while you're trying to talk to them. It's actually the move that gets me MORE undivided attention from our guests, not less.

And honestly? Picture it: we cut the cake, and the whole room roars—half for us, half because Georgia just scored. That's a memory. That's a story.

You're the priority. Always. The TVs are for them, and they'll be off the second you want them off. Just say the word.

...You already told the caterer to route the game to the main screen, didn't you?

I knew I loved you for a reason.
